body:
_Migrated from issue #1219, filed 2026-07-29._

Found while investigating #991. Filing separately because it is a real cost on its own, and its link to that report is **not** confirmed.

## What the code does

`CWASync:pullLibraryProgress` (`koreader/plugins/cwasync.koplugin/main.lua`) builds a path list via `getLibraryBooksForSync`. When the current view yields nothing, that falls back to `util.findFiles` over the **entire library root**, recursively, keeping every path `DocumentRegistry` can open.

`pullNextBook` then walks that list and, per book:

1. calls `getDocumentDigest(file_path)` — since #1189 (v4.1.23) this always opens the file, seeks 12 times and hashes, instead of reading KOReader's cached sidecar value;
2. issues a **blocking** `client.get_progress` round trip;
3. continues to the next book, recursing directly on the failure path with no `UIManager:nextTick` yield.

So a bulk sync is `O(books)` network round trips and `O(books)` file hashes, run back to back without returning to the event loop.

## Why it matters

On a large library this is minutes of wall clock with the UI thread pinned. On devices that power down wifi aggressively (Kindle in particular), a long enough run is exactly how the connection drops mid-sync and KOReader's network layer starts prompting to enable wifi.

Note the #1189 change did not create this shape — the per-book request loop predates it. It did raise the per-iteration cost: books that had been opened before used to answer from the sidecar cache and now get hashed like the rest. The change itself is correct and should not be reverted; the cached digest goes stale when the server's copy changes, which is the #991 bug it fixed.

## Directions worth weighing

- Batch the digest lookup: one request carrying many digests instead of one request per book. Needs a server endpoint.
- Yield to the event loop between books so the UI stays responsive and wifi keep-alive can run.
- Skip re-hashing when the file's size and mtime match what was recorded alongside the cached digest, so correctness is kept without paying for every book on every sync.

## Not yet measured

No device timing has been taken. Before building anything here, measure a real bulk pull on a large library and record per-book hash and request cost, so the fix targets whichever dominates.
title: KOReader bulk pull costs one blocking request plus a file hash per book, with no yield
